books.title: The Mystery of the Old Clock
books.author: Yently Kids
pages: In the corner of Grandpa's workshop stood an old clock that had not ticked for fifty years.
One rainy afternoon, Sara asked, 'Grandpa, why does the clock never tick?' Grandpa smiled and said, 'Let us find out.'
They opened the back of the clock and found a tiny brass key, a feather, and a note that said, 'For the one who listens.'
Sara put her ear close to the clock and listened. Very faintly, she heard a soft tick... tock... tick... tock.
'It was never broken,' whispered Grandpa. 'It was only waiting for someone patient enough to listen.'
Sara turned the little key, and the clock began to tick loudly and happily. It has ticked every day since.
Now Sara visits Grandpa every week, and the first thing she does is listen to the old clock's happy song.

books.title: The Little Inventor
books.author: Yently Kids
pages: Theo loved to invent things. His bedroom was full of boxes, wires, wheels, and bits of string.
One morning his little sister could not reach the top shelf where her toys were kept. 'Theo, help!' she cried.
Theo thought hard. Then he built a clever grabbing arm from a broom handle, a rope, and a kitchen tong.
He tested it again and again. The first time it dropped the toy, the second time it wobbled, but the third time it worked!
His sister clapped her hands. 'You are the best inventor in the world!' she said.
Theo smiled and wrote in his notebook: 'Invention number twelve: the Great Toy Grabber. It works!'

books.title: The Rainbow Bridge
books.author: Yently Kids
pages: After a big storm, a rainbow appeared over the river near Ella's house. It was the brightest rainbow she had ever seen.
Ella wished she could walk across it. To her surprise, the end of the rainbow touched the grass right in front of her.
She stepped onto the rainbow, and it felt soft and warm, like walking on a cloud. Up she went, higher and higher.
From the top, Ella could see the whole valley: the river, the fields, and her little house far below.
At the other end she found a meadow full of flowers that had never been seen before. She picked one to take home.
When Ella told her friends about the rainbow bridge, they did not believe her. But the strange flower in her hand proved it was real.

books.title: The Lost Treasure
books.author: Yently Kids
pages: Jake found an old map in his grandfather's attic. The map showed a big red X on a small island, and under it were the words: "The treasure is here."
The next morning, Jake took his little boat and sailed to the island. The sea was calm, and the sun was warm on his face.
On the island, Jake followed the map past tall palm trees and over sandy hills. At last, he saw a big rock with a red X painted on it.
Jake dug under the rock with his shovel. Clang! His shovel hit a wooden box. Inside the box were gold coins, jewels, and a note from his grandfather.
The note said, "The real treasure is a brave heart." Jake smiled and sailed home, proud of his adventure and ready to share the treasure with his whole family.
